reason: Court found judge erred by not giving tangible effect to Aboriginal background and requiring a link; substituted a community-based conditional sentence (majority).
Judge kept Gladue factors firmly in mind and showed restraint; custodial term upheld, only ancillary prohibition term shortened.
Judge fully examined Gladue and Ipeelee factors and treated them as mitigating; deterrence emphasis not an error; appeal dismissed.
No piecemeal approach; judge gave tangible effect to Gladue background by one-year reduction; ten-year sentence upheld.
Crown appeal allowed; suspended sentence replaced by two-year-less-a-day conditional sentence, though Gladue findings and rehabilitation were deferred to.
